# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 11 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**11:1** I give thanks to You, O Lord, for You have wrought wonders with dust, and with a vessel of clay You have shown great power.

**11:2** And what am I? I was taken from dust and fashioned from clay. I was shaped as a fountain of impurity and shameful nakedness,

**11:3** a mound of dust mixed with water, a habitation of darkness, a figure of clay that returns to dust

**11:4** at the appointed season and on the pathway of the dust-vessel. What shall the clay answer back, even that which is shaped by hand?

**11:5** What understanding shall it attain? You have wrought wonders with dust, and with a creature of clay You have shown great power.

**11:6** And how shall one born of woman be accounted before You? Kneaded from dust, his abode is the nourishment of worms.

**11:7** He is molded clay, and to dust he inclines once more. What shall the clay answer, the work of the hand?

**11:8** What understanding shall it attain?

**11:9** Yet You, You have placed in my mouth thanksgiving and upon my tongue a word of praise, the fruit of my lips in a place of singing,

**11:10** and I shall sing Your lovingkindness and Your power all the day long; continually shall I bless Your name.

**11:11** I shall declare Your glory among the children of men, and in the greatness of Your goodness my soul takes delight.

**11:12** And I know that truth is in Your mouth, and in Your hand righteousness, and in Your purpose all knowledge,

**11:13** and in Your power all might, and every glory is Yours.

**11:14** In Your wrath come all afflicting judgments, yet in Your goodness is abundance of pardon,

**11:15** and Your compassion extends to all the children of Your favor.

**11:16** For You have caused them to know the counsel of Your truth and given them discernment of Your wondrous mysteries.

**11:17** For Your glory's sake You have cleansed a mortal of transgression so that he might consecrate himself

**11:18** before You from every foul abomination and every guilt of faithlessness, to be united

**11:19** with the children of Your truth and in the lot of Your holy ones, to raise from the dust the worm of mortality

**11:20** to the everlasting assembly, and from a crooked spirit to Your insight,

**11:21** that he might stand in his place before You with the perpetual host and the spirits of understanding,

**11:22** to be renewed with all things present and to come, and with those who have knowledge in shared rejoicing.

**11:23** What is flesh beside all this? What creature of clay can perform wonders?

**11:24** From the womb he dwells in iniquity, and until old age in faithless guilt.

**11:25** I know that righteousness does not belong to a mortal, nor the blameless way to any son of man;

**11:26** to God Most High belong all righteous deeds, and the pathway of man is not firm of itself

**11:27** but only through the spirit God has shaped for him, to make perfect a way for the children of men,

**11:28** so that all His creatures may know the power of His might and the fullness of His compassion

**11:29** toward all the children of His favor.

**11:30** As for me, shuddering and shaking gripped me, all my bones shattered,

**11:31** and my heart dissolved like wax before the flame, my knees gave way like water rushing downhill,

**11:32** when I recalled my guilt and the faithlessness of my forebears, when the wicked rose against Your covenant

**11:33** and the worthless against Your word. Then I said: On account of my sin

**11:34** I am cut off from Your covenant. But when I called to mind the power of Your hand and the fullness of Your compassion,

**11:35** I took courage. I stood, and my spirit held firm against the blow,

**11:36** for I rested upon Your lovingkindness and the wealth of Your compassion. For You pardon iniquity

**11:37** and purify a mortal of guilt through Your righteousness.

---
*LOGOS notes: Column 11 is among the best-preserved of 1QHa. The hymn articulates the Qumran theology of radical divine grace contrasted with inherent human frailty. "Lovingkindness" for hesed (formal equivalent). "Children of Your favor" for bene retzonekha. The clay/dust anthropology echoes Genesis 2-3 and Job 10:9.*
